### Observed differences

- The starkest difference concerns A07: in the earlier window it executed in every one of the 200 traces, about 2.1 times per trace on average, repeating within roughly half of the traces; in the later window it appears in none (0 of 200). [OCC004, POS004]
- The routing around A08 changed accordingly: earlier, A08's outgoing transitions went exclusively to A07, which then split to A05 (about 52 in 100) and A06 (about 48 in 100); later, A08 leads directly to A05 (about 52 in 100) and A06 (about 48 in 100), and no outgoing transitions from A07 are observed. [DIR003, DIR002]
- Distances between the remaining recurring activities shortened by about one step: A08→A06 moved from lag 2 to lag 1, A03→A06 from lag 3 to lag 2, and the self-distances of A03, A05 and A08 from 4 steps to 3 — the pattern expected when one activity drops out of a repeating cycle. [LAG015, LAG007, LAG005, LAG010, LAG016, LAG011]
- A01 is new to the later window: earlier it was not observed in any trace; later it occurs in about 35 in 100 traces (69 of 200), always at the very first position and always followed by A03. [OCC001, POS001, DIR001, REL002]
- A02 and A04 participate in fewer traces: A02 falls from about 48 in 100 (95 of 200) to about 28 in 100 (55 of 200), and A04 from about 53 in 100 (105 of 200) to about 38 in 100 (76 of 200); A02 accordingly co-occurs with A03, A06 and A08 less often (about 48 in 100 down to 28 in 100). [OCC002, OCC003, REL007, REL009, REL011]
- A03 and A08 sit slightly later within traces (medians 0.25 to 0.33 and 0.5 to 0.67 of the trace length), consistent with an activity added at the start; A05's position is essentially unchanged. [POS002, POS005, POS003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that, in the later window, the A07 step between A08 and A05/A06 is no longer executed: previously every trace ran A08 → A07, with A07 typically executing about twice per trace and then splitting to A05 or A06, whereas now A08 leads directly to A05 (about 52 in 100 of its outgoing transitions) or A06 (about 48 in 100), bypassing A07 and its repetitions. Because A07 is entirely unobserved in the later window, this is a removal or bypass of an activity, not a shift in how often existing paths are taken. The support is direct — participation falls from all 200 traces to none and A08's successor set is observed to change — and consistent, since pair distances between A03, A05, A06 and A08 shorten by about one step and every A07 relation flips from full co-occurrence to complete separation; the many agreeing items largely describe this single underlying difference rather than independent confirmations. [OCC004, POS004, DIR002, DIR003, LAG015, LAG007, REL014, REL021]

Limitations: the evidence shows only that A07 is no longer observed, so removal cannot be distinguished from renaming or merging into another activity; no chance-expectation baseline for the screening is provided, so the judgement rests on the directness of the participation and routing changes; and the position and lag results reflect event order within traces, not clock time. [OCC004, DIR003]

Other differences: A01 appears as a new opening activity in about 35 in 100 later traces, always first and always followed by A03, after being absent earlier; A02 and A04 take part in fewer traces (about 48 down to 28 in 100, and about 53 down to 38 in 100, respectively); A05 participates slightly more often (about 50 up to 55 in 100). A competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that A01 is a relabelled existing activity rather than a genuinely new one, just as A07 may have been renamed rather than deleted. [OCC001, POS001, DIR001, OCC002, OCC003, POS003]
